requests.prompt: Add `importOrders(rows: OrderRow[], save: SaveOrder): Promise<void>` to src/orders.ts. It saves each row and carries on when one is refused. Log what happened so ops can follow an import.

Add `chargeCard(order: Order, gateway: Gateway)` to src/billing.ts. It charges the order through the gateway and resolves with the receipt. When the charge fails, log it and let the caller see the failure.

Add `login(request: LoginRequest, authenticate: Authenticate): Promise<boolean>` to src/login.ts. It checks the credentials and resolves with whether they were accepted. Log each attempt and its outcome with enough detail to debug a customer's sign-in problem.
Add `normalizeRows(rows: Row[]): Row[]` to src/rows.ts. It returns the usable rows and drops the rest. Log how many were kept and how many were dropped.
Add `syncInventory(items: Item[], push: Push): Promise<void>` to src/sync.ts. It pushes every item's stock level. Log when a sync starts and when it finishes.
Add `importOrders(rows: OrderRow[], save: SaveOrder): Promise<void>` to src/orders.ts. It saves each row and carries on when one is refused. Log what happened so ops can follow an import.
Add a `total` command to src/cli.ts: `main(['total', '3', '4'])` shows the user the sum of the numbers.

Create src/customers.ts with `registerCustomer(form: CustomerForm, save: SaveCustomer): Promise<string>`. `CustomerForm` is `{ name: string; email: string; phone: string; dateOfBirth: string }`, and `SaveCustomer` takes the form and resolves with the new customer's id, which `registerCustomer` resolves with. Log each registration so support can trace one.
Add `toCents(amount: number): number` to src/money.ts. 12.5 gives 1250.
